subject.title: Control UI: Config upgrade/hardening suggestions should apply changes automatically with before/after diff and user acceptance, not direct users to edit files manually

question: Which Control UI config and security recommendations may write user config, and what diff, confirmation, dismissal, audit, and restart policy must gate those writes?
rationale: The implementation shape is technically clear, but the authority for UI-originated changes to auth/security settings is a product and security boundary that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Approve allowlisted recommendation actions
options.body: Implement only vetted recommendation patches over the existing config RPC path, with explicit before/after acceptance and audit-safe confirmation.

options.title: Keep recommendations read-only
options.body: Leave hardening guidance as text and docs links so Control UI cannot mutate auth or security config from recommendation cards.

options.title: Defer fixes to doctor flows
options.body: Make CLI doctor or upgrade-scan the canonical fixer and have Control UI link to those flows instead of applying patches itself.

recommendation.title: Approve allowlisted recommendation actions
recommendation.body: Implement only vetted recommendation patches over the existing config RPC path, with explicit before/after acceptance and audit-safe confirmation.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision combines Control UI UX, setup guidance, and auth/security posture, and recent history points to steipete as the strongest product/security routing candidate.
